newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate tumbles to 9.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate tumbles to 9.6 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate tumbled to 9.6 percent on Tuesday from 11.1 percent as most lenders cut their prices amid strong liquidity in the banking sector.
Dealers put daily trade at a total 20.5 million kuna against supply of 72 million.
New deals amounted to 16.5 million kuna, almost half of which were call money loans granted at rates varying between a lower than usual 7.0 percent and the regular 8.0 percent.
One three-day loan was granted at 8.0 percent, while one-month deals were struck at 9.5, 10 and 13 percent, compared to 15 percent on Monday. Two-month borrowings were made at 17 and 18 percent.
Banks extended previous one week borrowings at 9.0 and 10.5 percent.

The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday weaker at 6.4008 from 6.3794 to the dollar and slightly weaker at 3.5679 from 3.5639 against the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
